messages:
Amanda: Heads-up — saw a Dedicated tenant hit their reserved throughput but still getting 429s during the midday spike. Looks like node-level concurrency cap is ejecting in-flight requests before our reserved throughput logic kicks in.
Raj: Can you paste the logs/errors? 429 from our quota layer or upstream runtime?
Amanda: Quota layer. Example header from a failed request: `X-Quota-Status: reserved_exhausted;inflight=128;limit=100;shared_available=0`
Tom: Ah that `inflight` vs `limit` mismatch is the issue — we enforce a hard node concurrency cap (per-tenant inflight <= N) even if tenant has reserved TPS on the pool. If the pool routes more requests, nodes still reject.
Kira: We always meant reserved throughput to guarantee capacity, not bypass node safety. But UXwise returning 429 with "reserved_exhausted" is confusing. Should surface "degraded_to_shared" or something when we fallback.
Lucas: Proposal: change policy so routing won't send more than node-concurrency-per-tenant, but when tenant > reserved_tps, allow a small per-tenant queue (e.g., 50 requests) at the router level and then spill to shared pool if router queue > 50. If both saturated -> 429 with clear reason.
Sasha: I like the router queue idea. Two concerns: 1) memory blowup if many tenants queue, 2) skewed fairness when one tenant monopolizes queue. We need per-tenant soft-limits and global queue caps.
Raj: For telemetry, we should add `dedicated.inflight_per_tenant`, `dedicated.router_queue_len`, `dedicated.fallback_to_shared_count`, and a label `reason=(reserved|node_cap|shared)` so we can chart the breakdown.
Amanda: Agreed. Also console UX: show a banner on tenant page "Requests are currently queued; serving from shared pool may increase latency" with counts and an option to toggle a per-tenant burst toggle (admins).
Tom: Implementation sketch: router receives request -> check tenant_inflight < node_concurrency_limit ? forward : enqueue up to ROUTER_QUEUE_MAX_PER_TENANT -> else try route_to_shared_pool (if allowed by policy) -> else return 429. Add header: `X-Redwood-Quota: status=queued;pos=12;queue_max=50` or `X-Redwood-Quota: status=fallback_shared;latency_penalty_ms=120`.
Kira: Small nit: header names should be short. Maybe `X-RWQ: s=queued;p=12;qm=50` to save bytes. But keep full names in logs.
Lucas: Rollout plan: feature flag `router-tenant-queue` on by default for 10% tenants, enable telemetry, run for 48h, then 100% with a 2-day ramp if no regressions. Add AB test to measure token-per-cost delta.
Sasha: Also add an alert: `dedicated.tenant_queue_p99_time > 2000ms` -> paging oncall. We don't want long tail queuing to be silent.
Raj: I'll add the metrics to the metrics catalog and dashboards: chart `dedicated.fallback_ratio` over time + by-tenant heatmap. Console should show a per-tenant time-series for "fallback to shared" and "queued" count.
Amanda: Who picks up the code change? @Tom for router, @Raj for metrics+dash, @Kira for console copy and toggle UI, @Lucas for rollout doc. Slack thread is the authority for decisions.
Tom: I'll open a PR with the queue implementation. Pseudoconfig in the PR:
```
router:
  tenant_queue_max: 50
  tenant_queue_global_max: 20000
  allow_fallback_shared: true
  headers:
    queued: "X-RWQ: s=queued;p=%pos%;qm=%max%"
```

Raj: I'll wire up `dedicated.router_queue_len` and `dedicated.fallback_to_shared_count` in telemetry agent. Will add labels `tenant_id` and `region` for triage.
Kira: I'll draft the console banner copy and make the admin toggle default-off for early rollout. Copy: "We are temporarily queueing requests for this tenant and serving some traffic from the shared pool. This may increase latency and cost. Toggle to allow short bursts."
Sasha: Good. One more ask: quota-bot, can you create an incident ticket template for when fallback ratio spikes > 10% for > 30m?
quota-bot: Created ticket RW-INC-4321 with runbook link https://internal/runbooks/dedicated-fallback. Assigned to eng-oncall. :white_check_mark:
Amanda: Thanks. If PRs land this week we can start the 10% flag flip early next week. I'll update the rollout doc when things are ready.
Raj: I'll add dashboard panels and a short alert to prod-monitoring.
Tom: On it — will make sure header emitted and logs annotated.
Amanda: Great work team. Follow-ups: PRs, metrics, console copy, rollout doc. Ping here when done. :thumbsup:
